open_points.subject: canonical identity ordering for flow edges and constants
open_points.text: “Lists whose order carries no meaning are sorted before hashing — ports by (`direction`, `name`), nodes by `node_id`, edges in the edge order of A05, constants by (`to_node`, `to_port`) — so the same content in another order has the same identity”
open_points.question: How are ties broken when distinct guarded edges have the same A05 endpoint-order key, or distinct constants target the same port, so reversing them cannot change `flow_version_id`?
options: Add canonical bytes of the whole edge or constant as a final sort key
Include guard facts or constant value facts as explicit tie-breakers
Treat tied distinct items as a composition refusal
open_points.default_guess: Use the canonical bytes of the whole item as the final tie-breaker.

open_points.subject: SpooledFile identity
open_points.text: M22 says “equal facts are the same spooled file”, while State 5 says “A SpooledFile is named by its producing position alone (SpooledFileKey)” and `read_spooled_file` omits digest, size, media type and disclosure class from the lookup identity.
open_points.question: Is a SpooledFile's identity its producing position alone, or all M22 facts including its content and class?
options: Producing position alone
All M22 meaning facts
Producing position plus content digest
open_points.default_guess: Use the producing position alone, as the later State 5 API explicitly requires.

open_points.subject: trial execution failure detail
open_points.text: `sandbox.execute_function` returns “a bounded `failure_detail` otherwise”, but TrialExecution M07 has no `failure_detail` field and `try_implementation` returns only “outcome, output digests, pass or `output_mismatch`”.
open_points.question: What happens to a sandbox failure detail during a trial or admission execution?
options: Store it on TrialExecution and return it under A07 masking
Return it only from an explicit try but do not persist it
Discard it for all trial and admission executions
open_points.default_guess: Store the bounded detail on TrialExecution and expose it under the existing A07 masking rule.

open_points.subject: oversized value output during trial or admission
open_points.text: TrialExecution M07 permits detail code `value_too_large`, `record_trial_execution` writes StoredValues for value outputs, but `sandbox.execute_function` says “`stored_value_bytes_max` and the spool ceilings are not the sandbox's — `runs` and `store` apply them”.
open_points.question: Who checks `stored_value_bytes_max` for a successful sandbox value output during `try_implementation` or admission, and what TrialExecution outcome is recorded when it is exceeded?
options: `functions` records `contract_violation` with `value_too_large` and stores no output
`store` refuses the value publication, causing `internal_error`
The trial output may exceed `stored_value_bytes_max` and is retained another way
open_points.default_guess: Have `functions` record `contract_violation` with `value_too_large` and retain no output value.

open_points.subject: rollback target chronology
open_points.text: “Activate an earlier implementation of the slot's current contract version” and “Activate an earlier implementation admitted over the current corpus.”
open_points.question: What makes an implementation “earlier”: creation before the currently active implementation, an earlier activation in the slot's history, or merely any admitted implementation that is not current?
options: Its Implementation record predates the current implementation
It appeared in an earlier Activation record
Any admitted non-current implementation is eligible
open_points.default_guess: Treat any admitted non-current implementation of the current contract version as eligible.

open_points.subject: EffectAttempt resolution time
open_points.text: M26 has “`recorded_at`, `concluded_at`; `resolved_by`: the owner, when an `unknown` was resolved”, while State 5 says lifecycle changes update “a status, who decided or resolved or released and when, `concluded_at`”.
open_points.question: When an `unknown` attempt is resolved, does `concluded_at` retain the time the transport outcome became unknown, change to the resolution time, or is a separate resolution timestamp required?
options: Keep `concluded_at` and add `resolved_at`
Replace `concluded_at` with the resolution time
Keep `concluded_at` and record no resolution time
open_points.default_guess: Keep the original conclusion time and add a separate `resolved_at` timestamp.

open_points.subject: manifest instance-name uniqueness
open_points.text: “`service_instances`: at most one selected instance per service, by its manifest instance name”
open_points.question: What happens when a service manifest contains two instance entries with the selected instance name?
options: Reject the manifest as a mismatch
Use the first entry
Use the last entry
open_points.default_guess: Reject the manifest as a mismatch.

open_points.subject: bindings.check_installed_instances manifest validation
open_points.text: “an unreadable record, or one failing a check of the record itself (A08 rule 5), fails at its service”
open_points.question: Which A08 rule 5 checks are performed at startup when `check_installed_instances` has no operation name, binding ports or proposal with which to perform the operation-specific checks?
options: Check only the service-record envelope, duplicate capability names and selected-instance facts
Validate every capability independently
Validate only capabilities referenced by accepted bindings
open_points.default_guess: Check only service-level structure, duplicate capability names and the selected instance facts needed for credential-header collision checking.

open_points.subject: service base URL
open_points.text: An instance address is accepted when it is “an absolute `http` or `https` URL with a host”, and the request URL is “the `api_base_url` without a trailing `/` followed by the declared path”.
open_points.question: Are base URLs containing user information, a path prefix, query, fragment, percent-encoded authority text or noncanonical host forms valid, and exactly how are they joined and represented on the wire and in `request_digest`?
options: Allow only scheme, authority and an optional path prefix; reject user information, query and fragment
Allow any absolute URL and concatenate textually
Require an origin-only URL with no path, query, fragment or user information
open_points.default_guess: Allow an optional path prefix but reject user information, query and fragment, preserving the accepted textual authority for the request description.

open_points.subject: credential bytes in approval previews
open_points.text: A17 says “The kernel never puts [the credential value] into ... a preview ... or a response”, while an approval preview contains “the built request and the input values” and the request description includes required-header values verbatim.
open_points.question: What happens if an input value, URL component, required-header value or multipart content happens to contain the credential bytes verbatim?
options: Refuse before creating a preview
Withhold the affected preview content and show only `request_digest`
Interpret the prohibition as applying only to the credential-header field itself
open_points.default_guess: Refuse the pre-send operation without storing a preview containing the credential bytes.

open_points.subject: service_invoker.send_prepared_request effect class
open_points.text: `send_prepared_request` takes “One prepared request and the operation's effect class”, although `prepare_request` built that request from a ManifestOperation that already has an effect class.
open_points.question: What happens if the separately supplied effect class differs from the class of the ManifestOperation used to prepare the request?
options: Reject the call as `internal_error`
Store the effect class inside the prepared request and remove the separate argument
Use the separately supplied class without checking
open_points.default_guess: Bind the class into the prepared request and treat any mismatch as `internal_error`.

open_points.subject: masked failure_detail length
open_points.text: “a `failure_detail` whose class is above `open` ... is returned to an agent only as its length and that class”
open_points.question: Is the disclosed length measured in Unicode code points, UTF-8 bytes before truncation, or UTF-8 bytes after replacement and truncation?
options: UTF-8 bytes of the stored bounded detail
Unicode code points of the stored detail
Original untruncated source length
open_points.default_guess: Return the UTF-8 byte length of the stored, already bounded detail.

open_points.subject: tokens in responses
open_points.text: A16 says “No response carries a token”, while paging operations return “the next continuation token when more remain”.
open_points.question: Does the prohibition cover only owner and agent authentication tokens, or continuation tokens as well?
options: Only authentication tokens are prohibited
All tokens are prohibited, so paging must use another cursor representation
Continuation tokens may be returned only under another name
open_points.default_guess: Interpret the prohibition as applying only to authentication tokens.

open_points.subject: existing store compatibility
open_points.text: `open_store` says “the database schema, the content-addressed area and the spool area are created inside the data directory when absent” but gives no rule for an existing database with an older, newer, incomplete or corrupt schema.
open_points.question: What must `open_store` do with an existing incompatible or corrupt store, especially when A20 permits a new release to execute records created by an earlier release?
options: Run specified atomic migrations
Refuse startup without modifying the store
Attempt repair or recreate missing structures
open_points.default_guess: Refuse startup without modifying the store unless an explicit migration for that schema version exists.

open_points.subject: spool_file cleanup after a ceiling refusal
open_points.text: `spool_file` promises that on a ceiling refusal there is “nothing kept of that file or of any file that attempt spooled before”, while “A link or an I/O failure is `internal_error` with nothing kept of that file.”
open_points.question: If removing files already spooled by the same attempt fails while handling a ceiling refusal, which result is returned and what state may remain?
options: Return `internal_error` and stop the kernel after reporting it
Return `refused` even if earlier attempt files remain
Make the cleanup transactional so the stated refusal effect is guaranteed
open_points.default_guess: Return `internal_error`, preserve no record for the attempt files and stop the kernel so recovery can handle the incomplete filesystem state.
